<style id="hw-child-customstyle-inline-css">
#wpbf-mobile-search-toggle {
	color: #fff;
	display: none;
}

#searchform-1::-webkit-search-cancel-button{
	display: none;
	-webkit-appearance: none;
}


#main article p a:not(.button) {
	color: #f25621;
}

#main article p a:hover {
	font-weight: bold;
	color: #0a0a0a;
}

.qr-wrapper {
	position: fixed;
	right: 1rem;
	padding: 0.5rem;
	z-index: 600;
	height: 5.5rem;
	box-shadow: 0 4px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 10%);
	background-color: #7f32cd;
	border-radius: 1rem;
	font-family: Poppins,Inter,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,sans-serif;
	font-weight: 800;
	font-size: 1.125rem;
	line-height: 1.5rem;
	letter-spacing: -.00625rem;
	line-height: 1.25rem;
	display: flex;
	bottom: -10rem;
	transition: bottom 0.3s ease;
}

.qr-wrapper.visible {
	bottom: 1rem;
}

.qr-wrapper  .text{
	margin-left: 0.5rem;
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	width: 2.75rem;
	word-spacing: 2.75rem;
	color: #00e0ce;
}

.qr-wrapper img {
	max-height: 100%;
}

.qr-wrapper:hover {
	height: 8rem;
	cursor: none;
}

.qr-wrapper:hover .text {
	display: none;
}

.getapp-wrapper {
	position: fixed;
	left: 50%;
	transform: translateX(-50%);
	align-items: center;
	justify-content: center;
	padding: 0.5rem;
	z-index: 600;
	box-shadow: 0 4px 32px rgb(0 0 0 / 10%);
	background-color: #7f32cd;
	border-radius: 1rem;
	font-family: Poppins,Inter,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,sans-serif;
	font-weight: 800;
	font-size: 1.125rem;
	line-height: 1.5rem;
	letter-spacing: -.00625rem;
	line-height: 1.25rem;
	display: none;
	bottom: -10rem;
	transition: bottom 0.3s ease;
}

.getapp-wrapper.visible {
	bottom: 1rem;
}

.getapp-wrapper  .text {
	margin-left: 0.5rem;
	display: flex;
	align-items: center;
	color: #00e0ce;
	text-decoration:none;
}

#author-info {
	margin-top: 3rem;
}

#author-info h3 {
	font-size: 1rem;
	font-weight: 500;
}

#author-info > div {
	display: flex;
}

#author-info > div img {
	width: 64px;
	height: 64px;
	border-radius: 50%;
	overflow: hidden;
	margin-right: 1.5rem;
}
#author-info > div section {
	width: calc(100% - 64px - 1rem);
	padding-left: 1.5rem;
	border-left: 1px solid #eee;
}
@media screen and (max-width: 768px) {
	#wpbf-mobile-search-toggle {
		display: inline-block;
	}

	.widget_search {
		position: fixed;
		top: -180px;
		left: 20px;
		opacity: 0;
		width: calc(100% - 40px);
		z-index: -1;
		transition: top 0.3s ease, opacity 0.5s ease;
	}

	body.mobile-search-open #content {
		z-index: auto;
	}
	body.mobile-search-open .widget_search {
		top: 80px;
		z-index:9999;
		opacity: 1;
	}

	.qr-wrapper {
		display: none;
	}

	.getapp-wrapper {
		display: flex;
	}
}

    // URL of the JSON file
    const jsonUrl = 'https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/themes/page-builder-framework-child/city-mappings.json';

    // Get the page title and clean it up
    const pageTitle = document.title.toLowerCase().trim().replace(/-/g, ' '); // Replace hyphens with spaces in the title

    // Function to insert widget at the end of the post
    function insertHostelWidget(city, hostelUrl) {
        const postContent = document.querySelector('.entry-content.article-content') || document.querySelector('.entry-content');

        // Insert widget if the post content is found
        if (postContent) {
            const widgetHtml = `
                <div id="widget-cta-${city}" class="bottom-cta" style="background-color: #ffffff; padding: 20px; margin-top: 20px; text-align: center;">
                    <h2 style="text-align: center;">Looking for hostels in ${city}?</h2>
                    <a id="cta-link-${city}" class="bottom-cta" href="${hostelUrl}" target="_blank" rel="noopener">
                        <img src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/image-1.png" alt="Hostelworld Hostels" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto; margin-bottom: 20px;">
                    </a>
                </div>
            `;
            postContent.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', widgetHtml); // Append the widget at the end of the post
        } else {
            console.log('Post content not found. Could not insert the widget.');
        }
    }

    // Fetch the JSON file
    fetch(jsonUrl)
        .then(response => {
            if (!response.ok) {
                throw new Error('Network response was not ok');
            }
            return response.json();
        })
        .then(data => {
            let detectedCity = '';
            let hostelUrl = '';
            let bestMatchLength = 0;

            // Loop through the city mappings and detect the city based on the title
            for (const city in data) {
                const lowerCity = city.toLowerCase().replace(/-/g, ' '); // Replace hyphens with spaces in the city name for matching
                
                // Exact match using strict word boundary (to prevent partial matches)
                const cityRegex = new RegExp(`\\b${lowerCity}\\b`, 'i');
                
                if (cityRegex.test(pageTitle)) {
                    // Exact match should override everything
                    detectedCity = city;
                    hostelUrl = data[city];
                    break; // Stop if exact match is found
                }
            }

            // If no exact match is found, use a partial match with a minimum length of 4 characters
            if (!detectedCity) {
                for (const city in data) {
                    const lowerCity = city.toLowerCase().replace(/-/g, ' '); // Normalize city names by replacing hyphens with spaces
                    
                    // If no exact match, check for partial match but avoid very short city names (min 4 characters)
                    if (lowerCity.length >= 4 && pageTitle.includes(lowerCity)) {
                        if (lowerCity.length > bestMatchLength) {
                            detectedCity = city;
                            hostelUrl = data[city];
                            bestMatchLength = lowerCity.length;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            // If a city is detected, insert the hostel widget
            if (detectedCity) {
                insertHostelWidget(detectedCity, hostelUrl);
            } else {
                console.log("No matching city found.");
            }
        })
        .catch(error => {
            console.error('Error fetching the city mappings:', error);
        });
});

class="content" data-v-7da7fd7d><h2>Terms and Conditions</h2>
<p>Last updated: 30 September 2021</p>
<p>These are the terms and conditions that govern the use of coupons (“<strong>Coupons</strong>”) when making bookings through our booking services, whether through our websites, mobile websites, mobile applications or our booking engine which is integrated into third party websites (collectively the "<strong>Hostelworld Sites</strong>").</p>
<p>All references to "we", "us" or "our" refer to Hostelworld.com Limited ("<strong>Hostelworld</strong>"), the operator of the Hostelworld Sites. Your use of a Coupon to make a booking on the Hostelworld Sites is subject to these terms and conditions, our <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hosteltermsandconditions/"><strong>General Terms of Use</strong></a> for use of the Hostelworld Sites and our <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/securityprivacy/"><strong>Data Protection Notice</strong></a> (collectively the "<strong>Terms</strong>"). You agree to use your Coupon in accordance with and subject to the Terms. Any information on the Hostelworld Sites about how to participate or use Coupons forms part of the Terms. By participating, you agree to be bound by the Terms. You must comply with the Terms for a Coupon to be valid.</p>
<h2>About Hostelworld Coupons</h2>
<p>By integrating with <a href="https://www.talon.one/"><strong>Talon One</strong></a>, the world’s most powerful marketing promotion engine, we support a coupons system that can be used by you against a booking for any room rate type advertised by our hostel partners globally on the Hostelworld Sites with the exception of our “Pay Now” and “Change Booking” room rates.</p>
<h2>How to Use Your Coupon</h2>
<ol>
  <li>Log in to your Hostelworld account via any of the Hostelworld Sites.</li>
  <li>Search for your desired hostel property and select your chosen room(s)/dorm(s) and room rate type (i.e., Non-flexible Booking, Standard Flexible Booking etc.).</li>
  <li>Click on the “Book Now” button to proceed to our “Secure Checkout” page.</li>
  <li>On the Secure Checkout page, simply type the Coupon code into the promotional box in the booking field and the relevant discount will be automatically deducted from the final price of the chosen room(s)/dorm(s) and room rate type.</li>
  <li>Click the “Confirm” button to confirm your booking.</li>
</ol>
<h2>General</h2>
<ul>
  <li>Each Coupon is identified by a unique numeric code and each Coupon will have a different corresponding percentage (%) discount applicable to it.</li>
  <li>Each Coupon will be valid for a single use only. If you apply your Coupon to a booking and you later cancel your booking (in accordance with the hostel’s cancellation policy), the Coupon will no longer be valid.</li>
  <li>Each Coupon is valid for a limited time only and will expire on the date specified on the Coupon. Coupons cannot be replaced if lost or misplaced.</li>
  <li>Hostelworld reserves the right to modify or cancel any Coupon offer at any time and for any reason. Hostelworld reserves the right to cancel a Coupon if it reasonably suspects fraud or misconduct.</li>
  <li>Coupons can only be applied to bookings on the Hostelworld Sites. Coupons cannot be applied retrospectively to any booking. If you do not enter the Coupon code at the time of booking as specified above, the booking will not be eligible for the discount.</li>
  <li>Coupons will be denominated in EUR but can be used when paying in GBP or USD.</li>
  <li>Coupons are not transferable or exchangeable for cash and cannot be combined with any other coupon, voucher, offer, discount or promotion offered by Hostelworld.</li>
  <li>Hostelworld can transfer its rights and obligations under these Terms to another organisation but will ensure that the transfer does not affect your rights under these Terms.</li>
  <li>Hostelworld can amend the Terms for these reasons: if we have to make a change to comply with a law or regulation that applies to us; if we are making the Terms better or fairer for you; if we are protecting you or Hostelworld from fraud or other harmful activity by third parties; if the way our Hostelworld Sites work is changing and this means that we have a good reason to change the Terms to reflect this; if our costs have changed and we need to make a reasonable change to reflect this; or if we need to update our contact details.</li>
  <li>Hostelworld shall not be liable for any loss, damage or injury suffered or sustained (even if caused by negligence) as a result of accepting and/or using the Coupon, except for any liability which cannot be excluded by law. Hostelworld accepts no responsibility for late, lost or misdirected email or other communications. Hostelworld assumes no responsibility for any failure to receive a Coupon or for inaccurate information or for any loss, damage or injury as a result of technical or telecommunications problems, including security breaches. If such problems arise, then Hostelworld may modify, cancel, terminate or suspend the Coupon.</li>

English INR English INR Accommodation Explore Hostelworld Work With Us Download the App Help / Report Illegal Content Hostelworld Coupons Terms and Conditions Last updated: 30 September 2021 These are the terms and conditions that govern the use of coupons (“ Coupons ”) when making bookings through our booking services, whether through our websites, mobile websites, mobile applications or our booking engine which is integrated into third party websites (collectively the " Hostelworld Sites "). All references to "we", "us" or "our" refer to Hostelworld.com Limited (" Hostelworld "), the operator of the Hostelworld Sites. Your use of a Coupon to make a booking on the Hostelworld Sites is subject to these terms and conditions, our  General Terms of Use  for use of the Hostelworld Sites and our  Data Protection Notice  (collectively the " Terms "). You agree to use your Coupon in accordance with and subject to the Terms. Any information on the Hostelworld Sites about how to participate or use Coupons forms part of the Terms. By participating, you agree to be bound by the Terms. You must comply with the Terms for a Coupon to be valid. About Hostelworld Coupons By integrating with  Talon One , the world’s most powerful marketing promotion engine, we support a coupons system that can be used by you against a booking for any room rate type advertised by our hostel partners globally on the Hostelworld Sites with the exception of our “Pay Now” and “Change Booking” room rates. How to Use Your Coupon Log in to your Hostelworld account via any of the Hostelworld Sites. Search for your desired hostel property and select your chosen room(s)/dorm(s) and room rate type (i.e., Non-flexible Booking, Standard Flexible Booking etc.). Click on the “Book Now” button to proceed to our “Secure Checkout” page. On the Secure Checkout page, simply type the Coupon code into the promotional box in the booking field and the relevant discount will be automatically deducted from the final price of the chosen room(s)/dorm(s) and room rate type. Click the “Confirm” button to confirm your booking. General Each Coupon is identified by a unique numeric code and each Coupon will have a different corresponding percentage (%) discount applicable to it. Each Coupon will be valid for a single use only. If you apply your Coupon to a booking and you later cancel your booking (in accordance with the hostel’s cancellation policy), the Coupon will no longer be valid. Each Coupon is valid for a limited time only and will expire on the date specified on the Coupon. Coupons cannot be replaced if lost or misplaced. Hostelworld reserves the right to modify or cancel any Coupon offer at any time and for any reason. Hostelworld reserves the right to cancel a Coupon if it reasonably suspects fraud or misconduct. Coupons can only be applied to bookings on the Hostelworld Sites. Coupons cannot be applied retrospectively to any booking. If you do not enter the Coupon code at the time of booking as specified above, the booking will not be eligible for the discount. Coupons will be denominated in EUR but can be used when paying in GBP or USD. Coupons are not transferable or exchangeable for cash and cannot be combined with any other coupon, voucher, offer, discount or promotion offered by Hostelworld. Hostelworld can transfer its rights and obligations under these Terms to another organisation but will ensure that the transfer does not affect your rights under these Terms. Hostelworld can amend the Terms for these reasons: if we have to make a change to comply with a law or regulation that applies to us; if we are making the Terms better or fairer for you; if we are protecting you or Hostelworld from fraud or other harmful activity by third parties; if the way our Hostelworld Sites work is changing and this means that we have a good reason to change the Terms to reflect this; if our costs have changed and we need to make a reasonable change to reflect this; or if we need to update our contact details. Hostelworld shall not be liable for any loss, damage or injury suffered or sustained (even if caused by negligence) as a result of accepting and/or using the Coupon, except for any liability which cannot be excluded by law. Hostelworld accepts no responsibility for late, lost or misdirected email or other communications. Hostelworld assumes no responsibility for any failure to receive a Coupon or for inaccurate information or for any loss, damage or injury as a result of technical or telecommunications problems, including security breaches. If such problems arise, then Hostelworld may modify, cancel, terminate or suspend the Coupon. 	});

	const scrollHandler = () => {
		const bodyHeight = document.body.scrollHeight;
		if (bodyHeight > 2 * window.innerHeight) {

				document.querySelector('.qr-wrapper').classList.add('visible');

			document.removeEventListener('scroll',scrollHandler);
		}
		console.log(bodyHeight, window.innerHeight, document.documentElement.scrollTop);

			<h1 class="entry-title" itemprop="headline">Discover Down Under: your guide for backpacking Australia</h1><p class="article-meta"><span class="article-author author vcard" itemscope="itemscope" itemprop="author" itemtype="https://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Hostelworld Blog</span></span><span class="article-meta-separator"> | </span><span class="posted-on">Posted on</span> <time class="article-time published" datetime="2018-09-26T12:15:55+00:00" itemprop="datePublished">September 26, 2018</time><span class="article-meta-separator"> | </span></p>
		</header>

		<section class="entry-content article-content" itemprop="text">

			
			<p>Australia – the backpacker’s dream destination. With stunningly rugged landscapes, once-in-a-lifetime outdoor activities, bizarre wildlife and a nation of the most down-to-earth hosts you’re ever likely to meet, it’s easy to see why. But hold up.  Before you start buying cork hats and practising your best “G’day mate”, keep in mind that Australia is also massive and occasionally very remote. While no one wants to over plan their trip to the land of no worries, our backpacking Australia guide is packed with helpful tips, itineraries and recommendations from travellers who have backpacked around Australia to make your trip down-under as laid-back as possible.</p>
<h2>Contents</h2>
<ol>

<h2 id="best-time-to-visit-australia">The best time to visit Australia</h2>
<p><em>Recommended by <a href="https://www.shesatripblog.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Emily Kammerlohr</a></em></p>
<p>The best time to visit Australia totally depends on what you like. If you visit during the Australian winter, you’ll enjoy milder temperatures in the ‘Outback’ (central Australia) and great whale watching on the east coast. If you visit during the Australian summer, you’ll get to experience a quintessential <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney/Bondi" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Bondi</a> Christmas and the amazing New Year’s party in <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Sydney</a> Harbour. It’s totally up to you.</p>
<h3>Visiting Australia in spring/summer</h3>
<p>In Australia, spring is from September to November and summer is from December to February. If you’re looking to catch some sun, the Australian summer makes the PERFECT getaway from the freezing temperatures of the northern hemisphere. Why not spend your winter break working on your tan instead of crowding around the fire?</p>
<p>Summer in Australia is like nowhere else. The sun seems to shire eternally and the fun never stops. Temperatures in Sydney hover around 25°-30° Celsius, making it the perfect time to bask in the Bondi sun or catch a few waves in <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney/Manly" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Manly</a>. On the opposite coast, <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Perth/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Perth</a>‘s weather is just as amazing – boasting nearly infinite sunny days with temperatures in the high 20’s.</p>
<p>As Australian beach culture is such a big part of the national identity, if you’d like to surf with the locals in <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Byron-Bay/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Byron Bay</a>, find Nemo on the Great Barrier Reef, or discover koalas on the sandy trails of Magnetic Island, spring and summer is the perfect time for you to visit the great land ‘Down Under’.</p>
<p><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99799" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-summer-in-Australia-1316x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw summer in Australia ice cream" width="875" height="582" /></p>
<h3>Visiting Australia in autumn/winter</h3>
<p>In Australia, autumn is from March to May and winter is from June to August. So if you’re from the northern hemisphere, <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/winter-in-australia/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">the Australian winter</a> occurs during your summer holidays – at a time when the Australian climate is relatively mild. Australia is such a big country with so much to see, meaning that you’ll need at least a month to six weeks to see everything you’d like to, if not longer. But you don’t need to take a gap year to do this. Even if you’re still in university, the temperature in Australia during the winter makes it the perfect “summer vacation” destination.</p>
<p>Many people think that the Australian climate is too cold during the autumn or winter months, but unless you are south of Sydney, it’s not cold at all. In fact, with average temperatures in the mid 20’s during the winter in northern<a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/area/Queensland/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links"> Queensland</a>, you can sail <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/secret-things-to-do-in-whitsundays/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">the Whitsundays</a>, camp on Fraser Island, and explore the Great Barrier Reef – all with only a light jacket.</p>
<p>During the winter, the temperature in Sydney hovers in the mid-teens, but it’s not uncommon for sunny days to reach the low 20’s. Perth’s weather is often very similar, although at night the temperature can reach single digits, so it’s best to bring some warm pyjamas with you.</p>
<p>While you may spend a night or two shivering if you travel the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/region/Great-Ocean-Road/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Great Ocean Road</a> near <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Melbourne" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Melbourne</a> during the winter, you will be thankful for the break from the scorching Aussie sun when you make the trek to Uluru.</p>

<h2 id="visa-for-australia">Backpacker visa for Australia</h2>
<p><em>Recommended by <a href="https://www.instagram.com/schreurseline/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Eline Schreurs</a></em></p>
<p>If you want to visit Australia, you’ll need to apply for a specific visa. Thankfully, for every type of traveller, there’s also a type of visa and for most backpackers the following three types of visas a popular.</p>
<p>The most popular visa for Australia from the UK and Europe (plus many other parts of the world) is the Working Holiday visa. This Australian backpacker visa allows you to stay and work in Australia for one year. If you want to apply, you’ll need to meet some entry requirements: you must be aged 18 – 30 years old, have enough money of your own (around AUD $5,000/ EUR <span class="w8qArf"> </span><span class="LrzXr kno-fv">€</span>3,000), must not have a criminal convictions and be in good health (if you have travelled for longer than 3 months in a ‘high/medium health risk’ area, you’ll need a hospital to assess you). You’re only allowed to have this visa once in your life with one exception: if you complete 88 days of farm work on your first visa you can apply for a second one. Some other types of work are also allowed for a second-year visa, but farm work is the easiest.</p>
<p>If you’re not planning to stay this long or if you don’t want to work while backpacking Australia, you can also apply for a tourist visa. With this visa, you can stay for up to three months, but there are some restrictions regarding any criminal convictions in your own country. Overall, the requirements for this visa are less strict.</p>
<p>You can also apply for a long-stay tourist visa. This visa enables you to backpack around Australia for up to a year, but you will not be allowed to work during this time. You will also be required to prove that you have enough money to travel around Australia without having to work, as they do not want people working illegally on this visa.</p>
<p>There is also the option of a student visa or job-specific visa, but these are more difficult to obtain and require a lot of extra paperwork. I think the easiest one is the Working Holiday visa as it gives you so much time and the option to work if you run out of money, which is likely in Australia.</p>

<h2 id="travelling-around-australia">Travelling around Australia</h2>
<p><em>Recommended by <a href="https://www.instagram.com/schreurseline/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Eline Schreurs</a></em></p>
<p>There are many ways to get around in Australia: you can drive, take the bus and train or even fly from one place to another. Don’t forget when choosing your type of transport that Australia is immense.</p>
<h3>1. Driving in Australia</h3>
<p>Driving in Australia is fantastic – you have all the freedom you want. You can go from one place to another without having to think about anything else. Driving in Australia with a UK licence is easy as your licence is also valid – and they drive on the left-hand side of the road too. If you’re not from a country where they drive on the left, it’s going to take a bit more time to adjust. But after a while, you get the hang of it – just be careful at the roundabouts (which can be tricky).</p>
<p>When you decide to go on a <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/road-trip-australia/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">classic Australian road trip</a>, the most important thing to remember is: take your time. Driving from <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/sydney-vs-melbourne/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Sydney to Melbourne</a> does not look that far on the map, but it takes around 10 hours on the most direct route. However, I recommend you take your time and go for the scenic route along the coast, as it’s a bit longer but so beautiful.</p>
<p>You should also avoid driving at night; during the day you can at least see the native wildlife (like kangaroos and koalas) crossing the road but at night it’s much harder to react on time. Not only do you not want to kill one of these cute animals, but you also don’t want to risk your own life – kangaroos are especially big and can cause some serious damage to your car. While you’re driving around Australia, you will already see a lot of native animals lying dead at the side of the road so please drive carefully.</p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99804" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-driving-in-Australia-1400x788.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw driving in Australia" width="875" height="492" /></p>
<h3>2. Campervan and car hire</h3>
<p>There are many options for driving around Australia: you can <a href="http://www.cars.hostelworld.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">rent a car</a> and drive between hostels, or you can take a tent and camp at the many campsites. But I think the most relaxed way to drive around Australia is to buy or rent a campervan that you also can sleep in. There are different companies who rent vans like <a href="https://www.travellers-autobarn.com.au/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Travellers Autobarn</a> or <a href="https://www.wickedcampers.com.au/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Wicked Campers</a>.</p>
<p>If you’re in backpacking Australia for a long time, it may be a better idea to buy a van from other backpackers. In every hostel, you will see ads from backpackers selling their vans or cars, but before you agree to a deal with someone, make sure the car gets checked by an independent mechanic. Most of those vans are all pretty old, and you don’t want to break down in the middle of the Outback. Also, don’t forget to buy car insurance – most banks offer some excellent deals for backpackers. The Commonwealth Bank, for example, really helped me out with all my questions about this.</p>
<p><a href="http://www.cars.hostelworld.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Rent a car with Hostelworld</a></p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99803" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-van-hire-1167x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw van hire" width="875" height="656" /></p>
<h3>3. Public transport in Australian cities</h3>
<p>If you’re visiting one of the bigger cities like <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Sydney</a>, <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Melbourne" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Melbourne</a> and <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Brisbane/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Brisbane</a>, driving is not comfortable. There’s way too much traffic and you will often get stuck in a traffic jam. The best way to get around in a big city is by public transport. They each have buses, train and tram lines inside the city and a lot of various train lines that can take you outside the city. The public transport in Australian cities is fantastic: it’s almost always on time, with an option every 5 minutes and it is not too expensive. Every state uses their own public transport card. For public transport in Melbourne you need to buy a Myki card and top it up, and then you can use on all the different types of public transport. For Sydney public transport the pre-payment option is called the Opal card. You can use this card for everything in Sydney, such as ferries, trams, buses, etc. Also, on Sundays, you only need to pay a certain amount (like AUD $5) for public transport, and when you reach that limit, you can use the rest of the day public transportation for free. This is particularly interesting if you want to go for a day trip to the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Blue-Mountains/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Blue Mountains</a> or to <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney/Manly" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Manly</a> for example. You can top-up these cards with as much money as you want – but don’t make the mistake of putting too much on it because you cannot get it back.</p>
<h3>4. Backpacker buses in Australia</h3>
<p>The most popular way to travel around Australia is to take the ‘backpacker’ bus from one place to another. You can choose between two bus companies: <a href="https://www.premierms.com.au/PMS/pages/home/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Premier</a> and <a href="https://www.greyhound.com.au/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Greyhound</a>. The most significant difference between the two is the price; Premier is cheaper than Greyhound, but they have fewer options than Greyhound – and on Greyhound you also have Wi-Fi and phone charging points. However, both companies stop at the exact same places, so it’s simply a matter or availability and price.</p>
<p>Both these companies offer flexible passes, which means you can buy a pass for the whole East Coast (from Melbourne to <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Cairns/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Cairns</a>) and ‘hop on hop off’ whenever you want. In the high season, you should reserve your place on the bus well in advance or you’ll risk not having a seat at all.  When it’s low season, you’ll still need to reserve your seat, but you can often leave it to the last minute.</p>
<p>You can also buy different passes, such as from Sydney to Cairns or Brisbane. So, it really depends where you are, where you want to go to and how much time you have. Most of the backpackers start in Sydney and end up in Cairns (making the same stops in between like Fraser Island and <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/secret-things-to-do-in-whitsundays/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">the Whitsundays</a>), but there’s much more to see, so do your research before you buy a pass. You may even realise that buying a car is the better option for you. But if you don’t want the hassle of a car and insurance then the backpacker bus is the better way for you to see Australia.</p>
<h3>5. Budget airlines and trains in Australia</h3>
<p>If you’re in a hurry to get between destinations, then it’s probably better to fly or catch the train. For example, there’s a sleeper train from Sydney to Brisbane that covers the 14-hour journey overnight. Be warned though, the cheapest ticket is for a seat not a bed and it’s a pretty uncomfortable way to sleep. However, Australian trains are of a very high standard, especially the interstate XPT trains that run from Sydney.</p>
<p>If the idea of a long car ride (like the whopping 19-hour Brisbane to Cairns drive) really isn’t for you then flying is probably your best option. Australia has multiple budget airlines, such as Jetstar, Tigerair and Virgin Australia. If you book far enough in advance, you can often get a good price. Alternatively, if you know which domestic flights you will need before booking your international ones, why not pop them on the same ticket? Qantas do a Walkabout Pass which means you can fly with them everywhere in Australia for a fraction of the price.</p>

<h2 id="australia-travel-costs">Australia travel costs</h2>
<p><em>Recommended by <a href="https://www.shesatripblog.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Emily Kammerlohr</a></em></p>
<p>Australia is expensive – but backpacking Australia on a budget is still possible. You don’t need to sacrifice safety or comfort in the land ‘Down Under’ to have a magnificent adventure. It’s typical of backpackers in Australia to compare budgets and frustrations about the high cost of living in this Oceanic paradise, but if you’re careful it’s possible to leave Australia with money left over.</p>
<h3>1. Currency in Australia</h3>
<p>The currency in Australia is the Australian Dollar. It’s denoted by the dollar sign “$” same as the American and Canadian Dollar. While exchange rates can vary daily, as of August 2018, the average conversions are as follows:</p>
<p>American Dollar vs. Australian Dollar:</p>
<p>$1.37 / $1</p>
<p>Euro vs. Australian Dollar:</p>
<p>€1.56 / $1</p>
<p>British Pound Sterling vs. Australian Dollar:</p>
<p>£1.74 / $1</p>
<p>Canadian Dollar vs. Australian Dollar:</p>
<p>$1.05 / $1</p>
<h3>2. Cost of flights to Australia</h3>
<p>The costs of flights to Australia can vary greatly, but a backpacker on a budget should always keep their eyes open for sales and deals. For example, certain airlines often have “end of year” sales or major sales around holidays.</p>
<p>Another way to secure cheap airfare to Australia is by waiting for error fares. An error fare is when an airline mistakenly publishes a fare that is well below market price – sometimes as low as 90% off. The only downside is that error fares are not always honoured and typically have restricted dates.</p>
<p>From the UK, you should expect to pay an average of AUD $900 to AUD $1,200 for a flight out of London without any special deals. From Germany, flights tend to run about AUD $1,400, no matter the airport or season. From Canada, flights can vary depending on the season and city of departure. For example, flying from Toronto in September can cost roughly AUD $1,500, while flying from Vancouver in May can be AUD $1,300.</p>
<p>From the USA, flight availability and prices vary greatly as the market becomes more competitive, with non-stop flights from San Francisco, Dallas, Houston, and Los Angeles consistently priced under AUD $1,000.</p>
<h3>3. Backpacking Australia: daily budget</h3>
<p>Before setting off to backpack Australia, you should think about what experiences you would like to splurge on. This is because while the day-to-day costs while travelling Australia on a budget can be kept relatively low, experiences such as camping under the stars at Uluru or sailing the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/secret-things-to-do-in-whitsundays/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Whitsunday Islands</a> can be expensive, depending on how you choose to experience them.</p>
<p>If you already know which bucket list items you are willing to spend more money on, you can factor the costs into your original budget and not worry about blowing through all your cash when it is time to experience them.</p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99812" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-baby-kangaroo-1313x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw baby kangaroo" width="875" height="583" /></p>
<h3>4. Australian hostel costs</h3>
<p>In larger cities like <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Sydney</a> and <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Melbourne" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Melbourne</a>, a bed in an 8-person dorm typically goes for roughly AUD $20–$35 a night, while in smaller cities like <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Cairns/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Cairns</a> or <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Byron-Bay/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Byron Bay</a>, you can stay cheaper, typically for under AUD $20–$25 a night.</p>
<p>Your daily costs can be reduced significantly by staying a hostel that includes breakfast and has free Wi-Fi, as even if the fee to access these amenities is small (often less than AUD $5), if purchased every day, they can add up quickly.</p>
<h3>5. Eating and drinking</h3>
<p>Alcohol is expensive in Australia due to import costs and taxation, so do not be surprised to see the average city cocktail come in around AUD $25 or more. Buying your alcohol at the local bottle shop (called a “bottle-o” to Aussies) is always cheaper than going out. A staple of the Australian backpacking experience is “goon”, which is a very inexpensive bagged wine.</p>
<p>A sit-down meal at your average restaurant can cost anywhere from AUD $25 -$40 (even for a burger and chips), which is why many backpackers choose to purchase groceries at supermarkets like Woolworths or Coles and cook a meal in their hostel instead.</p>
<p>When you’re on an extreme budget (and want to experience an authentic Aussie treat) stop by the hardware store Bunnings Warehouse for their $1 sausage sizzle every Sunday.</p>
<h3>6. Sightseeing</h3>
<p>The great thing about Australia is that there are so many wonderful things to see and do that are completely free. For example, whilst climbing the Harbour Bridge in Sydney is well over AUD $200, you are welcome to walk across it for free. Many museums in Sydney and Melbourne are also completely free and you can take in the overwhelming nature of Northern Queensland and the Outback without paying a cent through your own hikes and scenic drives. See our recommendations for things to do in Australia below.</p>

<h2 id="best-places-to-visit-in-australia">Best places to visit in Australia</h2>
<p><em>Recommended by <a href="https://www.instagram.com/schreurseline/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Eline Schreurs</a></em></p>
<p>Australia is one of the most amazing countries in the world. Even if you live here for a year, you’ll still struggle to visit all the places that are on your bucket list.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3>1. Uluru and the Outback</h3>
<p>The most famous landmark in Australia is Uluru. This sacred rock is in the middle of the Outback, as Australia’s vast desert interior is called. It takes a couple of days to get there by car and is expensive, but anyone you speak to who has visited it says it is worth it. Most backpackers are drawn to the Outback because of the promise of adventure: you’ll drive for days without encountering anybody else, sleep under the most beautiful starry sky you’ll ever see and feel at one with nature the whole time.</p>
<p><strong><span style="font-size: 14pt;color: #ff6600"><a style="color: #ff6600" href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Alice-Springs/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Book your hostel in Alice Springs</a></span></strong></p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99806" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-Uluru-1313x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw Uluru" width="875" height="583" /></p>
<h3>2. Melbourne and the Great Ocean Road</h3>
<p>If you’re starting your trip on Australia’s east coast, then your first stop should be <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Melbourne" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Melbourne</a>. Known for its chilled-out vibes and numerous hipster bars, there’s so much more to this city than places to drink. Your Melbourne backpacker itinerary should include Hosier Lane, with the most beautiful graffiti you’ll ever see, and architecture and book fans shouldn’t miss the amazing State Library of Victoria. If the weather is lovely, take a walk next to the Yarra River and make your way through the Kings Domain to the impressive Shrine of Remembrance war memorial. You also need to visit Queen Victoria Market, especially on a Sunday when there’s also a lot of street musicians and food stands around. Your hostel can help you arrange a backpacker tour around Melbourne if you’re interested in a guided experience of the city.</p>
<p>Heading out of Melbourne, you shouldn’t miss the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/road-trip-australia/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">iconic road trip</a> along the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/region/Great-Ocean-Road/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Great Ocean Road</a>. This two or three-day trip includes many stunning beaches and rock formations; the most famous one is the Twelve Apostles, which are slowly disappearing due to erosion, so you better hurry up if you want to see them.</p>
<h3>3. Melbourne to Cairns: backpacking east coast Australia</h3>
<p>Most of the backpackers opt for the classic east coast itinerary when visiting Australia for the first time, taking in most key destinations from Melbourne to <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Cairns/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Cairns</a>. You can squeeze this whole route in if you’re only backpacking Australia for 3 weeks – or take time and stretch it out across 3 months. Listed below are some of the key landmarks and attractions you should include when doing this classic Australian backpacking route.</p>
<h3>4. Sydney and the Blue Mountains</h3>
<p>If you’re planning on backpacking the east coast of Australia, you will definitely stop in <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Sydney</a> for a few days. This lively and vibrant city has an incredible range of beaches – and, of course, you must take a selfie with the Opera House and spend an afternoon chilling in Hyde Park. You can climb the iconic Sydney Harbour Bridge if you’re looking for a high-adrenaline adventure, but you also shouldn’t miss other landmarks like Taronga Zoo, Luna Park, Circular Quay and the Rocks and many more.</p>
<p>If you’re more into <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/guide-to-the-best-beaches-in-sydney/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">beaches</a>, then you’ll discover the city has a wide range of options. Take the ferry (which I highly recommend, especially at night) and visit <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney/Manly" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Manly</a> and Shelly beach. Both beaches are amazing and the surfy suburb of Manly is also worth a visit. Of course, you should visit Sydney’s most famous beaches: <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Sydney/Bondi" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Bondi Beach</a> (as seen on the reality TV series <em>Bondi Rescue</em>) and Palm Beach (the setting for TV soap opera, <em>Home and Away</em>). The easiest way to make new friends in Sydney is to go to a <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/best-bars-in-sydney/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">backpacker bar</a>, such as Scary Canary near Darling Harbour, and start talking to other people. Most of these bars are entwined with hostels, like the awesome <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hosteldetails.php/Wake-Up-Sydney-Central/Sydney/1704" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Wake Up! hostel</a> bar – so choose the right one and you will have a bunch of friends in no time.</p>
<p>If you fancy a day trip from Sydney, then you shouldn’t miss the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Blue-Mountains/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Blue Mountains</a> National Park. You can visit the breathtaking Three Sisters rock formation and enjoy a long walk in the park, to absorb all the natural beauty. Book a hostel and stay overnight – or even for a couple of days – as you will find so many new and amazing things to do here.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/c/sydney" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Check out our Sydney guide</a></p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99807" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-Sydney-Harbour-Bridge-1313x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw Sydney Harbour Bridge" width="875" height="583" /></p>
<h3>5. Byron Bay</h3>
<p>If you’re travelling by bus from Sydney, then your next stop will probably be <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Byron-Bay/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Byron Bay</a>. Known to be a little hippie stoner town, its reputation has grown so much that people say the moment you drive into the city you become high. Maybe it was like this years ago but now it’s much more of a tourist-friendly destination. It’s still wonderful and has serious hippy vibes, but it’s also more commercial. Make sure to visit the lighthouse at the top, it will give you a fantastic view.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/things-to-do-in-byron-bay/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Incredible things to do in Byron Bay</a></p>
<h3>6. Gold Coast</h3>
<p>The next stop is something entirely different: <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Surfers-Paradise/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Surfers Paradise</a>. The main reason backpackers stop here is to party: join a pub crawl your hostel and you’ll probably end up in Sin City, the club where the bartenders work in their underwear. But there is so much more to the <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/region/Gold-Coast/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Gold Coast</a> than partying. Immerse yourself in the natural wonders of the regions, such as the very Instagramable sunflower fields in Allora or lush waterfalls at Tallebudgera Valley.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/things-to-do-on-the-gold-coast/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Amazing things to do on the Gold Coast</a></p>

<h3>7. Brisbane</h3>
<p>Close to the Gold Coast is the Queensland state capital, <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Brisbane/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Brisbane</a>. Some people are surprised at how different it is to Sydney and Melbourne, with its own unique vibe. Brisbane has the most beautiful botanic gardens, where you can wander around in for hours. Head to the South Bank to visit the beautiful Gallery of Modern Art and the National Library, then chill by the river in the sunshine or grab a drink and enjoy the sunset.</p>
<p>When you’re in Brisbane, you must not forget to go shopping.  This city has a beautiful and historical centre, with many cool places and shops. Find yourself a new outfit and go dancing, because there are a lot of great places to party. Brisbane is a vibrant city with an interesting history.</p>
<p><span style="color: #ff6600"><strong><span style="font-size: 14pt"><a style="color: #ff6600" href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Brisbane/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Find a hostel in Brisbane</a></span></strong></span></p>
<h3><span style="color: #000000">8. Noosa</span></h3>
<p>After all this partying, it is time to relax a bit again – and there’s no place better than <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Noosa/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Noosa</a>. This little town has the most stunning beaches. Please stop and stay here for a couple of days, enjoy the coastal walk, take a sunset boat tour, and go kayaking on the Everglades. Whatever you do here, it’s going to be marvellous.</p>
<p><strong><span style="color: #ff6600;font-size: 14pt"><a style="color: #ff6600" href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Noosa/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Find a hostel in Noosa</a></span></strong></p>
<h3>9. Fraser Island and the Whitsundays</h3>
<p>Next up on your backpacking route for Australia’s east coast is one of the most amazing places in the whole world. Head to the coastal town of <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Rainbow-Beach/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Rainbow Beach</a> to catch the barge to Fraser Island. Not only is it the world’s largest sand island, is also is the home to the beautiful Lake McKenzie and the sparkling Champagne Pools. It also a great place for spotting whales and other sea life (along with the occasional dingo). Fraser Island is indeed a magical place; when the sun goes down, head to the beach with your towel, lay back and watch the stars. It’s the most impressive thing you will ever see.</p>
<p>Your next stop is further along the coast. The little town of <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Airlie-Beach/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Airlie Beach</a> is another starting point for an iconic Australian attraction: the Whitsunday Islands. Book a tour with a boat (there are many options) and you’ll find yourself transported to the most picturesque and natural white beaches and blue ocean. It will feel like you’ve ended up on a postcard. Go snorkelling, hire a paddle board or simply relax.</p>
<p><a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/secret-things-to-do-in-whitsundays/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Discover secret things to do in the Whitsundays</a></p>
<p><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" class="aligncenter wp-image-99815" src="https://www.hostelworld.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2018/09/Backpacking-Australia-@exploreshaw-island-car-1313x875.jpg" alt="Backpacking Australia @exploreshaw island car" width="875" height="583" /></p>
<h3>10. Magnetic Island and Cairns</h3>
<p>After the Whitsundays, it’s time for Magnetic Island. To get here, you first have to travel to <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Townsville/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Townsville</a>; this city has a range of great hostels, so you can either stop here for a night or head straight to the island to stay at one of the hostels here. While you’re here, don’t miss the chance to hire one of the island’s iconic pink hire cars (for some Barbie realness). Drive down to Bungalow Bay Koala Village and pet these cute animals at this beautiful sanctuary. After this head, to the beach for a relaxing afternoon and enjoy the sunset with a box of ‘goon’ and your friends.</p>
<p>By now you’ll almost be in <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/Cairns/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Cairns</a>, but if you want you can make one more to stop when backpacking the east coast of Australia: Mission Beach. This is the place try skydiving if you’re keen – if not, proceed directly to Cairns and its famous <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hosteldetails.php/Gilligan-s-Backpacker-Hotel-and-Resort-Cairns/Cairns/5201" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Gilligan’s Backpacker Hotel & Resort</a>. This hostel is renowned for its legendary party nights – but don’t miss the amazing day trips you can try from here: the Great Barrier Reef, Daintree Rainforest, Cape Tribulation plus exploring the beautiful waterfalls around Cairns.</p>

<h3>11. Northern and Western Australia backpacking route</h3>
<p>Most of the backpackers only travel the east coast on their first trip, but there’s another side to this incredible country. If you want to see the real Australia, you must go to the west coast. It’s rougher with no big cities but it’s different and (in my opinion) more authentic experience of Australia. If you want to drive yourself around the west coast, then I recommend that you <a href="http://www.cars.hostelworld.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">rent a 4WD sized car</a>. This is the only way to go to all the cool places – as the west coast has some places that are seriously off-the-beaten-track.</p>

<h3>12. Darwin</h3>
<p>If you want to go from the ‘Top End’ of Australia and head down the west coast, then <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Darwin/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Darwin</a> is your first stop. It’s one of the biggest cities you’ll experience on this itinerary – and it is boiling there. You’ll find most backpackers in the hostel pool because the sea is full of deadly box jellyfish… and crocodiles. Yup, that’s right, crocodiles. If you happen to like crocodiles, don’t go looking for them on the beach but head to Crocosaurus Cove, an aquarium where you’ll have the opportunity to get up close and feed them.</p>
<p><strong><span style="color: #ff6600"><a style="color: #ff6600" href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Darwin/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links"><span style="font-size: 14pt">Find a hostel in Darwin</span></a></span></strong></p>
<h3>13. Lake Argyle and National Parks</h3>
<p>Once you head across the border into <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/hostels/area/Western-Australia/Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Western Australia</a>, you’ll reach Lake Argyle, which has the most beautiful sunsets. Take a boat trip around the lake and swim with non-dangerous crocodiles. After Lake Argyle, you can drive to Purnululu National Park, which has fantastic rock formations; it’s worth reading up on Indigenous history in this area. After this, drive to King Leopold Range National Park and try one of the walks here or just relax and enjoy the nature.</p>

<h3>14. Broome</h3>
<p>By now you will arrive in the third biggest town on this backpacker itinerary, <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Broome/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Broome</a>. There’s not a lot to see in Broome (it has roughly four streets to the town) but it’s worth stopping for Cable Beach, which has some amazing sunsets. You can even ride a camel on the beach.</p>

<h3>15. Karijini National Park</h3>
<p>The west coast of Australia has some of the most beautiful national parks, including Karijini National Park. The best thing to do here is walk through the big red rock formations – it’s so amazing, you feel like you’re in a movie.</p>
<h3>16. Shark Bay</h3>
<p>If you like sea animals, then you need to stop at Shark Bay (also known as <a href="https://www.hostelworld.com/findabed.php/ChosenCity.Monkey-Mia/ChosenCountry.Australia" target="_blank" rel="noopener" class="post links">Monkey Mia</a>). There’s a show with wild dolphins, where you can learn a lot about their habits and some lucky people can feed the dolphins. There’s also the option of taking a boat tour so you can experience more of the local sea life.</p>

<h3>17. Kalbarri National Park</h3>
